basics.name: Linkage and mechanism datasets from research papers (LINKS, the 3M planar linkage dataset, MechBench, MechVerse)
basics.url: LINKS: https://decode.mit.edu/projects/links/ (project page), code at https://github.com/ahnobari/LINKS, data at https://huggingface.co/datasets/ahn1376/LINKS-10M. 3M dataset: https://par.nsf.gov/biblio/10635249 (NSF public-access record of the ASME paper). MechBench: https://dynamo-web.pages.dev/ and https://github.com/Mayank3108/DYNAMO. MechVerse: https://mechverse.pages.dev/ and https://huggingface.co/datasets/Mayank-p3108/MechVerse
basics.resource_type: GitHub repo or dataset (four separate machine-learning research datasets, each with a paper; not a reference work)
basics.cost: Free (LINKS, MechBench and MechVerse downloads are free; the 3M dataset paper is in an ASME journal, which is normally paywalled, but NSF lists a public-access record; where to download the 3M data itself could not be found [uncertain])
basics.license: Mixed. MechVerse: CC BY 4.0 (Hugging Face card: reuse, including commercial, allowed if you cite the paper, link back and say what you changed). LInK (the follow-up code and data release for LINKS): CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike). LINKS repo: no LICENSE file found (raw LICENSE returned 404), and the LINKS-10M Hugging Face card gives no licence, so reuse terms are unclear [uncertain]. MechBench (DYNAMO repo): no LICENSE file found [uncertain]. 3M dataset: licence not found [uncertain]. Linking to the project pages and papers is always fine; reusing their pictures in the encyclopedia is only clearly allowed for MechVerse (with credit)
basics.year: LINKS: 2022 (arXiv 30 Aug 2022; ASME IDETC 2022); the LINKS-10M Hugging Face copy was uploaded August 2025; follow-up LInK paper May 2024 (TMLR 2024). 3M dataset: ASME Journal of Mechanical Design vol. 147 no. 4, published April 2025. MechBench: arXiv 15 Sep 2025 (DYNAMO paper). MechVerse: arXiv 14 May 2026 (under review); Hugging Face dataset last updated 19 June 2026
basics.access_barrier: none to read the project pages and arXiv papers; to use the data you need programming (Python notebooks, NumPy/Parquet/NPZ files) and a lot of disk space (LINKS-10M is about 24 GB to download; MechVerse is a large Video.zip). The 3M dataset paper sits behind the ASME paywall (NSF public-access record only), and a public download link was not found
basics.image_license: MechVerse video clips: CC BY 4.0 (same as the dataset). LINKS/LInK figures and demo: no separate image licence; LInK repo is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 [uncertain whether that covers LINKS figures]. MechBench renders and meshes: not stated [uncertain]. arXiv papers carry their own per-paper licences (MechVerse HTML shows CC BY 4.0)
basics.authority_level: academic peer-reviewed (LINKS: ASME IDETC 2022 conference paper from MIT DeCoDE Lab and MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab; 3M dataset: ASME Journal of Mechanical Design 2025 from Stony Brook University; MechBench: arXiv preprint from Purdue University, peer review status not confirmed [uncertain]; MechVerse: arXiv preprint marked 'Under Review', Purdue University)

coverage.covers: Mostly randomly generated or synthetic machine-learning training data, not named mechanism types. LINKS: 100 million one-degree-of-freedom planar linkages (flat bar-and-pin mechanisms, 1-DOF planar linkages) with up to 20 joints, plus 1.1 billion traced paths (coupler curves); the Hugging Face copy LINKS-10M holds 10 million mechanisms plus 20,000 test items. 3M dataset: nearly 3 million single-DOF four-bar, six-bar and eight-bar linkages with open and closed coupler curves, including sliding-joint (prismatic) variants; a follow-up paper uses a curated 33-type subset of about 1.2 million. MechBench: 693 synthetic gear assemblies (spur, helical, double-helical/herringbone, rack and pinion, internal ring gears, bevel, worm and screw gears, planetary), 2 to 7 parts each, with meshes and motion paths. MechVerse: 21,156 short video clips of 1,357 moving assemblies in 141 categories; 904 are everyday hinged objects from PartNet-Mobility (doors, laptops, drawers) and 453 are CAD mechanisms (cam and follower, elliptical trammel, engine piston, four-bar linkage, Hobson joint, universal joint, and about 114 one-off 'unique mechanisms')
coverage.organisation: By dataset file and number, not by name or purpose. LINKS is organised by graph structure (topology) and simulated path, with a 'curated' subset that removes most circles and arcs. The 3M dataset is grouped by linkage family (4-, 6-, 8-bar) and mechanism type. MechBench is one flat set of numbered assemblies (Assembly####.npz) with gear-type illustrations. MechVerse is grouped into three difficulty tiers (Easy: 1-2 independent parts; Medium: 3-8 coupled parts; Hard: 10-50 parts) and by category name. None of these can be browsed by someone who does not know the terms; they are meant for loading into code
coverage.scope_match: low to medium. They are about linkages, gear trains and cam mechanisms (in scope), but they are machine-learning training data with numbered or random examples rather than a catalogue of named clever connection types; no latches, snap fits, clutches, ratchets or adhesives. MechVerse's CAD category list and MechBench's gear-type list are the most usable parts
coverage.taxonomy_used: LINKS: graph topology of simple kinematic loops built by a special 'J operator' (no named families). 3M dataset: number of links (4-, 6-, 8-bar) and named sub-types (e.g. Watt and Stephenson six-bars and prismatic variants; 33 types in the curated subset [uncertain on exact names]). MechBench: 13 gear-type labels on its project page (spur, helical spur, double helical spur, rack and pinion, helical and double helical rack and pinion, internal involute, helical and double helical internal, bevel, helical bevel, worm, screw gear) plus planetary systems. MechVerse: 3 complexity tiers, 141 categories (19 PartNet-Mobility object classes plus CAD classes such as CamAndFollower, EllipticalTrammel, EnginePiston, FourBarLinkage, HobsonJoint, UJoint, UniqueMechanism), and a motion vocabulary (rotation, translation, rotation+translation, planar; clockwise, opening, extending, sliding, tilting and so on)
coverage.example_types: Four-bar linkage (crank-rocker); Six-bar linkage (Watt and Stephenson types) [uncertain on which are named in the 3M paper]; Eight-bar linkage; Slider-crank (linkage with a sliding, prismatic joint); Multi-loop planar linkage with up to 20 joints (path-generating linkage); Spur gear pair; Helical and double-helical (herringbone) gears; Rack and pinion; Internal (ring) gear; Bevel gear; Worm gear; Crossed-axis screw gear; Planetary gear set; Cam and follower; Elliptical trammel (trammel of Archimedes); Engine piston (slider-crank); Hobson joint (Hobson's joint, a bent-pin shaft coupling); Universal joint (U-joint, Cardan joint)
coverage.making_methods: General engineering and robotics design automation (computer-aided mechanism design and machine learning). Not aimed at 3D printing, CNC or woodwork, although the MechBench meshes/STEP files and MechVerse OBJ files could be printed
coverage.item_count: LINKS: 100,000,000 mechanisms and 1.1 billion coupler curves (10,000,000 plus 20,000 test items in the LINKS-10M copy). 3M dataset: about 3,000,000 mechanisms. MechBench: 693 gear assemblies. MechVerse: 21,156 clips of 1,357 assemblies in 141 categories (453 CAD mechanism assemblies)
coverage.special_behaviours_covered: torque-limiting: no; self-locking: no (worm gears are included in MechBench but self-locking is not discussed; LINKS actually filters out 'locking' linkages, meaning ones that jam, which is a different idea); hand-release only: no; one-way/ratchet: no; indexing/detent: no (no Geneva drive found in the named categories) [uncertain, since MechVerse's 114 'unique mechanisms' are not listed]; over-centre: no; compliant: no (all rigid-body); print-in-place: no; gear trains/gearboxes: yes for MechBench (13 gear types plus planetary sets) and partly MechVerse (gear trains named among its CAD assemblies); powered connectors: no; adhesive types: no
coverage.entry_structure: LINKS: joint start positions, links as a list of connected joint pairs (edges), fixed (ground) joints, a solve order, and the traced target curve as numbers. 3M dataset: joint coordinates, mechanism type and a simulated coupler curve (also as images for a VAE) [uncertain]. MechBench: per-assembly NPZ file with part point clouds, part mask, motion type, a coupling matrix saying which parts drive each other, motion centres and axes, and 36 frames of 3D transforms; full meshes and STEP files on Google Drive. MechVerse: 2-second video (32 frames at 16 fps), a still input image, a structured text prompt (which parts move, which are fixed, motion type, direction, speed, what drives what), and OBJ 3D files

usefulness.beginner_friendliness: low. The pages are written for machine-learning researchers (terms like coupler curve, chamfer distance, SE(3) trajectories, contrastive learning). There are no plain-English explanations of what each mechanism does. The exceptions are the LINKS web demo (a simple browser tool to build and animate linkages and try curve-matching challenges) and the MechVerse and MechBench project pages, which show short animations
usefulness.has_images: yes, on the project pages and papers: rendered gear-type pictures (MechBench), rendered assemblies and dataset charts (MechVerse), and path/linkage diagrams (LINKS). They are research figures, not labelled teaching diagrams
usefulness.has_animations: yes. MechVerse is itself 21,156 animation clips (Unity renders of mechanisms moving) with an interactive viewer on its project page; MechBench/DYNAMO project page shows predicted versus true gear motion; LINKS has an interactive browser 'Linkage Designer' (https://decode.mit.edu/links/) for drawing and simulating linkages, and LInK has a Hugging Face alphabet-drawing demo (it returned HTTP 503 when checked)
usefulness.gaps: No names or plain descriptions for most items (LINKS mechanisms are random graphs); nothing on joints, fasteners, snap fits, latches, clutches, ratchets, compliant or print-in-place parts, powered connectors or adhesives; no design rules, dimensions, materials or tolerances; very large downloads needing code; licences unclear for LINKS, MechBench and the 3M set; 3M dataset download location not found
usefulness.good_for_entry_links: poor for single entries: there are no stable per-mechanism web pages. Best used as 'further reading' links from a family overview, e.g. the LINKS web demo https://decode.mit.edu/links/ from a 'linkages' page, the MechBench project page https://dynamo-web.pages.dev/ from a 'gear types' page, or https://mechverse.pages.dev/ for mechanism animations
usefulness.reusable_data: structured and machine-readable: LINKS-10M as Parquet on Hugging Face (licence not stated [uncertain]); MechBench as processed NPZ files in the DYNAMO GitHub repo plus meshes and STEP on Google Drive (no licence file [uncertain]); MechVerse as JSON splits plus Video.zip on Hugging Face under CC BY 4.0 (reusable with credit). The category lists themselves (MechVerse's 141 categories, MechBench's gear types) are short and could be copied as vocabulary with a citation
usefulness.maintained: LINKS: static since 2022, with a new Hugging Face copy in August 2025; project page and demo online in 2026. 3M dataset: published 2025, still cited by 2026 follow-up papers. MechBench: released September 2025. MechVerse: new (May 2026), Hugging Face data updated June 2026. All pages opened successfully on 2026-09-25 except the LInK Hugging Face demo (HTTP 503)
usefulness.ideas_to_borrow: (1) MechVerse's three-tier difficulty scale (independent parts / a few coupled parts / many coupled parts) is a neat way to label mechanism complexity in the encyclopedia. (2) MechVerse's controlled motion vocabulary (rotation, translation, rotation+translation, planar; clockwise, opening, extending, sliding, tilting) could seed the flow chart's 'what motion do you need' question. (3) MechVerse's structured description of each mechanism (fixed parts, moving parts, what drives what, direction, range) is a good template for an entry's 'how it moves' box. (4) MechBench's side-by-side gear-type illustration is a good model for a gear family overview. (5) The LINKS 'draw a path, find a linkage that traces it' demo is a fun interactive idea to link to for linkages
usefulness.design_rules_given: no. No clearances, tolerances, strengths or torques. The only numbers are geometric (joint coordinates, gear counts, motion ranges such as 180, 360 and 720 degrees for the speed variants)
usefulness.generator_or_parametric: partly: LINKS code (Python) generates and simulates random planar linkages, and the LINKS web demo lets you build and simulate a linkage in the browser; LInK synthesises a linkage to trace a drawn curve. MechBench and MechVerse are fixed collections, not generators
usefulness.file_formats: LINKS: Parquet (Hugging Face), NumPy files, Jupyter notebook, Python code. LInK: NumPy, Python, Google Drive downloads. MechBench: NPZ (processed), 3D meshes and STEP files (full set on Google Drive). MechVerse: MP4-style video clips in Video.zip [uncertain on exact video format], JSON prompts and splits, OBJ 3D assets. Papers as PDF/HTML
usefulness.terminology_value: low to medium: correct academic names for linkage and gear types (four-bar, six-bar, coupler curve, rack and pinion, internal involute gear, worm, screw gear, Hobson joint, elliptical trammel), but no definitions, aliases or translations
usefulness.decision_support: none for choosing a mechanism. The research tools do 'inverse design' (given a path you want, find a linkage that traces it), which is a kind of automated selector for linkages only, but it needs code or the demo, not a flow chart
usefulness.derived_from_or_overlaps: MechVerse's easy tier is built from PartNet-Mobility (SAPIEN) everyday articulated objects; its CAD set and MechBench come from the same Purdue group (Karthik Ramani's lab) and share authors. LInK (2024) builds on LINKS. The 3M dataset follows earlier Stony Brook four-bar datasets (Deshpande and Purwar 2019-2020) and is used by later papers (e.g. a 2026 autoregressive-transformer paper). Related but separate: 'A Dataset for Mechanical Mechanisms' (about 9,000 sketch images with descriptions, arXiv 2409.03763) and Lipson's image-based planar linkage dataset (arXiv 2510.03308). Cite the original papers for each
